---
title: "Contribute"
---
The collection is open to contributions of two kinds, and to corrections. The maintainers review each one; once accepted, it is credited and listed in the changelog of the release that adds it.

## Data from a physical test

A test is useful for judging a simulator when its setup can be rebuilt. A submission contains:

1. the measured quantities, as numbers, in SI or with their units stated;
2. the soil: what it is, its grain size, and its density in the test;
3. the bed: container size, fill depth, and how the soil was placed;
4. the tool or vehicle: shape, size, mass where it matters;
5. the motion: how the tool moved or was loaded, and how fast;
6. what was measured, with which instrument, and anything known about its accuracy;
7. what is not known, said plainly;
8. the source (a report, a paper, or the laboratory that ran the test) and permission to share the data.

## A script that runs a virtual experiment

A virtual experiment script mirrors one of the tests hosted here in a simulator. A submission states:

1. which test it mirrors (the record id on the test's page);
2. the simulator and its version;
3. the inputs chosen where the record is silent (the choices left to the user on the test's card), with the reason for each;
4. its output, in the quantity that was measured (for a load-penetration test, the load on the tool against its penetration).

## Corrections

A point that looks wrong, a better scan of a page, or an answer to one of the open questions (under [Project records](../records/index.qmd)): give the page and, for a point, where it is on the scan. For a value that looks wrong, the [Report a problem with a value](https://github.com/uwsbel/terramechanics-reference-data/issues/new?template=report-a-value.yml) form asks for the release, the record id, the figure or table, the printed and PDF pages, and the evidence.

## How to send it, and how it is reviewed

Open an issue on the project's [GitHub repository](https://github.com/uwsbel/terramechanics-reference-data). The maintainers check data against its source, and run a script to confirm that it gives the output it states. Accepted contributions enter under the same rules as everything else here: every number traceable to its source. Feedback not meant to be public goes to Dan Negrut, [negrut@wisc.edu](mailto:negrut@wisc.edu).
